channel.title: Low Tide Radio
channel.description: Nene Ocampo is sixteen and would rather be anywhere than Astoria. Her grandfather has the keys to a shut-down AM station above the boat yard, two hundred watts of transmitter and nobody to talk to. What they put on the air at six every morning turns into the thing the town sets its clocks and its tides by.

item.title: Chapter 18 — Six in the Morning, Still
item.description: The most recent chapter. Chapter 19 is on the drawing board. 26 pages, reading right to left.

item.title: Chapter 17 — What the Tide Line Keeps
item.description: Winter, and the first chapter drawn entirely in the new room over the chandlery. 30 pages, reading right to left.

item.title: Chapter 16 — Night Programme
item.description: Nene takes the ten o’clock hour, alone, and finds out who is awake. 28 pages, reading right to left.

item.title: Chapter 15 — Relay
item.description: A second aerial on the ridge, put up by six people and a borrowed truck. 22 pages, reading right to left.

item.title: Chapter 14 — The Bar at the Mouth
item.description: Why the Columbia bar is the reason a two-hundred-watt station still matters. 26 pages, reading right to left.

item.title: Chapter 13 — Small Craft Advisory
item.description: A November bar crossing, read out live because nobody else will. 24 pages, reading right to left. Content note: Peril at sea. Nobody drowns.

item.title: Chapter 12 — Storm Watch
item.description: Back after seven months, and the show has to be rebuilt from a cold start. 28 pages, reading right to left.

item.title: The Nine O’Clock Bell
item.description: A standalone about the harbour bell and the man who rang it for thirty years. Drawn left to right for a print anthology, and it reads on its own — no chapter before it is needed. 24 pages, reading left to right.

item.title: Chapter 11 — Sign-Off
item.description: The arc ends with the station running and one of its two people not in it. 32 pages, reading right to left. Content note: A hospital stay, on and off page.

item.title: Chapter 10 — Interference
item.description: A new LED sign at the marina wipes out the band from four blocks away. 26 pages, reading right to left.

item.title: Chapter 9 — A Letter From Neah Bay
item.description: Somebody 120 miles north is listening on a skip signal after dark. 24 pages, reading right to left.

item.title: Chapter 8 — Sponsors
item.description: The hardware store offers forty dollars a month and an opinion. 18 pages, reading right to left.

item.title: Chapter 7 — The Six O’Clock Tide
item.description: A crab boat starts planning its morning around the broadcast. 22 pages, reading right to left.

item.title: Chapter 6 — Dead Air
item.description: The arc opener, and the chapter that catches a new reader up without a recap page. 28 pages, reading right to left.

item.title: Chapter 5 — First Broadcast
item.description: Six in the morning. Tide table, weather, one song. Four people hear it. 30 pages, reading right to left.

item.title: Chapter 4 — Lolo’s Tape Box
item.description: Forty reels labelled in a hand Nene can read and a language she cannot. 26 pages, reading right to left.

item.title: Chapter 3 — Two Hundred Watts
item.description: What that number covers at night, and what it does not. 20 pages, reading right to left.

item.title: Chapter 2 — The Tower on Cannery Hill
item.description: Two hundred feet of guyed mast, and the reason the licence never lapsed. 22 pages, reading right to left.

item.title: Chapter 1 — Static
item.description: Nene is handed a key ring and a building with a hole in the roof. 34 pages, reading right to left.
